argument:
The bull's strongest refinement is profitable year-on-year execution in the latest quarter, rather than backlog alone. Revenue growth of 13.2%, profit growth of 19.8% and margin of 12.2% genuinely establish that point. They do not answer how the RM2.371bn backlog will translate into financed cash returns when 89.1% exposure remains EPCC and debt/FCF are unknown.

Sequential revenue declining from RM270.5m to RM155.9m demonstrates variable delivery, not failed projects. A buyer at the 48.00x vendor multiple must nevertheless accept uncertain timing and cash conversion without evidence of financing adequacy. Electricity-sales growth complements the book but does not neutralise its dominant exposure. The extended chart adds entry caution; waiting needs no assertion of a new delay or cost overrun.
key_points: Future backlog cash conversion and funding are unanswered.
EPCC concentration and extended pricing constrain immediate entry.
rebuttal_to_previous: Annual profit growth answers a purely undelivered-backlog objection. It does not rebut the financing and timing concern; the bull explicitly leaves both open, so observed quarterly profitability alone is insufficient to justify buying.
